Dear FOI Team,

Re: my FOI request of 2 July 2026, “Great House Farm, Llandough | Cardiff Castle Furniture”

New information has come to light about historical and descriptive names for the site, including “Llandough Home Farm” in the 1881 census image. Please rerun or extend the relevant searches for my original request using the terms below where they help identify records in your holdings. The request remains limited to recorded information about furniture, furnishings, antiques, fixtures, heirlooms and other movable property originating from the site, including inventories, acquisition or transfer records, provenance, photographs and correspondence. This message does not ask you to determine ownership or the merits of any claim.

The site is Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr beside St Dochdwy’s Church at Llandough-juxta-Penarth, near Penarth and Cardiff, Vale of Glamorgan: HER GGAT02038s, NPRN 20182, grid reference ST16707335. The later development address is Church View Close, [postcode redacted]. Please distinguish it from the separate Llandough Farm opposite the hospital, Llandough-juxta-Cowbridge and nearby Llandow or Aberthin. Cowbridge-area records and the Great Houses at Llandow and Aberthin are outside scope.

Farm and building forms: “Great House Farm”; “Great House Farm, Llandough”; “Great House Farm (GGAT02038s)”; “Great House”; “Great house”; “Greathouse”; “Tŷ Mawr”; “Ty Mawr”; “Ty-mawr”; “Ty Mawr Farm”; “Ty Mawr (Great House)”; “Ty Mawr, Penarth Road, Llandough”; “Cydfin Farm”; “Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm, (107 a.)”; “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm”; “Cedfin”; “Cydwin”; “Cedwyn”; “Cedfyn”; “Cefin”; “Llandough Home Farm”; “Land Doc Home Farm”; “R-W-S-S Farm / Reese’s Farm”; “Llandough Church Farm”; “Church Farm”; “former Great House Farm”; “a 3.4 acre site located adjacent St. Dochdwy Parish Church”; and “LLANDOUGH FARM (Ideal Homes Wales)”. Descriptive phrases include “an 800-year-old house”, “the ten-roomed house”, “ancient Welsh house” and “the farm / the whole of the farm”.

The census image reads “Llandough Home Farm”; “Land Doc Home Farm” is a competing reported transcription, and “R-W-S-S Farm / Reese’s Farm” is a lead that does not appear on the checked page. “Cydwin” and “Cedwyn” are unverified research leads; “Cedfyn” and “Cefin” are search forms without a confirmed primary occurrence. “Church Farm” and “Llandough Church Farm” are source-specific terms with unresolved identity. The 1994 Ideal Homes Wales plan uses “LLANDOUGH FARM” for the development site, while another Llandough Farm is a separate farmstead. None of these terms alone proves a record concerns this site.

Estate and surrounding-area forms: “Cedwyn Estate”; “Cydwin”; “Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm, (107 a.)”; “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm”; and “Cwm Cydfin Wood”. “Cedwyn Estate” is the family’s working name for the wider historic estate, not an established period name. The Bute catalogue range 1552 - 1824 is not a specific date for its Ty Mawr wording; the 1824 Stewart survey records “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm”; and “Cwm Cydfin Wood” appears in a 1902 Bute sale catalogue. These forms are search aids, not proof of shared boundaries or title.

Locality forms: “Llandough-juxta-Penarth”; “Llandough near Penarth”; “Llandough near Cardiff”; “Llandough, Penarth”; “Llandough, Cardiff”; “Llandough”; “Landoche-juxta-Cardif”; “Llandough / Leckwith”; “Penarth Road, Llandough”; “Urban District of Penarth”; “Llandochau”; “CF64”; and “Church View Close, [postcode redacted]”. “Landoche-juxta-Cardif” is a manor locator, not proof that a particular holding in a record is this farm. “Llandough / Leckwith” is neighbouring parish and manorial context, not another farm name.

The detailed nomenclature pages are:

Please tell me which terms, indexes, catalogues or record series were checked and identify anything newly found within the original request’s scope. Please keep this separate from other requests.

Yours sincerely,

Requester

Environmental Information Regulations Reference No:  2026/224580

Thank you for your request for information about:

  *   Whether HSE or HM Factory Inspectorate holds any of the following for the period 1 October 1988 to 30 June 1989:

1. any notification received about demolition or building operations at this site under the legislation then in force, including the name of the contractor and of the person or company for whom the work was done;
2. any record of an inspector's visit, inspection, enforcement action or reported incident at the site in that period;
3. any index or register entry showing that such a notification or visit was recorded, even if the file itself no longer exists.

If no information is held, please tell me:
(a) which record series and systems were searched, including any historic paper indexes;
(b) the retention period that applied to such notifications and inspection records in 1988–89; and
(c) whether any transfer or disposal record exists for them.

Your request was received on November 3rd 2026 and I am dealing with it under the terms of the Environmental Information Regulations 2004.

I can confirm that your request is being dealt with under the Environmental Information Regulations 2004 (EIR).  However I must advise you that following a search of our paper and electronic records, I have established that the information you requested:

Is not held by the Health & Safety Executive
a) Record systems COIN, F10 and Content Manager were searched
(b) The current retention period is 7 years, thus any records from 1988-89 are no longer available
(c) There are no transfer or disposal records
General guidance on how the Health & Safety Executive deals with requests under the Freedom of Information Act and Environmental Information Regulations can be found on the HSE website at http://www.hse.gov.uk/foi/index.htm

If you are unhappy with the decisions made by HSE you may ask for an internal review within two calendar months of the date of this letter by writing to me.

Dear Requester



Freedom of Information Request – FOI/2026/16



I am writing in response to your recent application for information held by the Library (Ref FOI/2026/16) received here at the Library on 16 October 2026 and stated the following:



“This is a new request under the Freedom of Information Act 2000. It is
outside the scope of FOI/2026/09 and its internal review, which
concerned Bute series including D153 and D205 and the 1877
transaction. It is also separate from my enquiry of 27 September and
follow-up of 10 October 2026 on D153/1–8.

PLEASE NOTE: DUPLICATE PLACE AND FARM NAMES IN GLAMORGAN
Glamorgan has two parishes called Llandough, and each had a farm
called Great House.
IN SCOPE: Llandough-juxta-Penarth (Llandough near Penarth and
Cardiff), hundred of Dinas Powys. Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr stood
beside St Dochdwy's church, approx. ST 168 733.
OUT OF SCOPE: Llandough-juxta-Cowbridge (Llandough near Cowbridge),
and the Great Houses at nearby Llandow and Aberthin. For example,
"Manors of Llandough and St Mary Church" (Penrice and Margam Estate
Records, 1619–1704) appears to be the Cowbridge Llandough; please
confirm if you know otherwise.
Please do not send or rely on records for the Cowbridge-area places.
If an entry says only "Llandough" or "Great House" and the parish
cannot be told, please say so rather than assume.

Part 1 — S7, Survey of the lands of William Herbert, kt, dec., in the
lordships or manors of Dinas Powys, Cogan, Llandough and others,
January 1610.
Please tell me:
(a) Whether S7 contains an entry for Great House or any holding in
Llandough-juxta-Penarth, and the folio.
(b) The name of the holder or tenant recorded, the tenure (freehold,
copyhold, leasehold) and any rent or acreage given.
(c) Whether S7 is digitised or filmed, and the cost of a copy of only
those folios.

Part 2 — Cardiff MSS on Microfilm (CARDMFS), filmed 1980–1984.
Glamorgan Archives (ref 2026/4097b) identified Bute X.6(12), abstracts
of payments and receipts by the Bute trustees, 1877 (copy), at Cardiff
Library.
Please tell me:
(a) Whether Bute X.6(12), or any Bute X.6 item, is on the CARDMFS
microfilm, and the reel and frame reference.
(b) If so, how I can obtain a copy of the entries relating to
Llandough-juxta-Penarth or Daniel Thomas, and the cost.

Part 3 — A lease of Great House said to date from 1667.
The family's account (not yet supported by a document) is that the
Williams family took Great House, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, in 1667 on
a lease for 999 years. Great House is described in published sources
as a freehold of the Vaughan family from the 16th to the late 18th
century, after which it came to the Bute estate. Please tell me
whether the Bute Estate Records, including the Herbert and Windsor
family papers within them, or any other NLW collection, hold:
(a) Any lease, counterpart lease, assignment or enrolment,
c.1660–1675, of Great House or any messuage in
Llandough-juxta-Penarth, to any person named Williams, or for a term
of 999 years (or any other long term).
(b) Any later deed, abstract of title, schedule or rental that recites
or refers to a lease of Great House for 999 years or for a long term.
(c) The conveyance or other instrument by which the Bute estate (or
the Windsor family before it) acquired Great House from the Vaughan
family or its heirs, with its date and reference, and whether it
recites any lease or tenancy then outstanding.
(d) Any Vaughan of Llandough family papers, and where they are held if
not at NLW.

If you consider any of this reasonably accessible by other means under
section 21, please say exactly where and how.

January 1610.

(a) Whether S7 contains an entry for Great House or any holding in
Llandough-juxta-Penarth, and the folio.
(b) The name of the holder or tenant recorded, the tenure (freehold,
copyhold, leasehold) and any rent or acreage given.
(c) Whether S7 is digitised or filmed, and the cost of a copy of only
those folios.
